question: Describe exactly what the following Resources handlers do, with file:line excerpts: DeleteResourceTypeCommandHandler (does it soft-delete instances, hard-delete the type, in what order, and is there a single SaveChangesAsync or several), DeleteResourceInstanceCommandHandler or equivalent (soft or hard delete), and GroupDeletedHandler (how it deletes types/instances, whether via ExecuteDeleteAsync, and whether SaveChangesAsync is called). Also report whether ResourceInstance has a soft-delete flag (property name, file:line) and whether any EF global query filter excludes soft-deleted instances (file:line).
claim:
DeleteResourceTypeCommandHandler (backend/src/Modules/Resources/ThingsBooksy.Modules.Resources.Core/Features/DeleteResourceType/DeleteResourceTypeCommandHandler.cs) first soft-deletes all resource instances of the type via a bulk ExecuteUpdateAsync (IDeleteResourceTypeCommandDataProvider.SoftDeleteInstancesAsync, which sets DeletedAt/UpdatedAt and bypasses the query filter with IgnoreQueryFilters), then removes the ResourceType entity from the DbSet (RemoveResourceType, EF-tracked hard delete, relying on DB cascade for ResourcePropertyDefinitions), and finally calls SaveChangesAsync exactly once. The bulk ExecuteUpdateAsync executes immediately/independently of SaveChangesAsync (it is its own SQL statement), so there is one explicit SaveChangesAsync call in the handler (for the RemoveResourceType tracked-entity delete), after the instances have already been soft-deleted by the bulk update. Order: (1) soft-delete instances via ExecuteUpdateAsync, (2) hard-delete the type via tracked Remove + single SaveChangesAsync.

DeleteResourceInstanceCommandHandler (backend/src/Modules/Resources/ThingsBooksy.Modules.Resources.Core/Features/DeleteResourceInstance/DeleteResourceInstanceCommandHandler.cs) performs a SOFT delete: it loads the tracked ResourceInstance entity, calls the domain method instance.Delete(_clock.CurrentDate()) (which sets DeletedAt, per ResourceInstance.cs:46), then calls _dataProvider.SaveChangesAsync once. No hard delete/ExecuteDeleteAsync is used.

GroupDeletedHandler (backend/src/Modules/Resources/ThingsBooksy.Modules.Resources.Core/Events/Handlers/GroupDeletedHandler.cs) is an IEventHandler<GroupDeleted> reacting to a group-deleted domain event from ManagementGroups. It: (1) soft-deletes all ResourceInstances for the group via a bulk ExecuteUpdateAsync (IgnoreQueryFilters + Where DeletedAt==null, SetProperty DeletedAt/UpdatedAt to now) — this is a direct SQL bulk statement, not a SaveChangesAsync-tracked save; (2) hard-deletes all ResourceTypes for the group via ExecuteDeleteAsync (also IgnoreQueryFilters, no Where on DeletedAt, comment states DB cascade removes ResourcePropertyDefinitions) — also a direct bulk SQL statement; (3) then looks up the GroupReadModel by Id, and only if found, removes it from the tracked DbSet and calls _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken) once (line 46) — this is the only explicit SaveChangesAsync call in this handler, and it only fires conditionally when a GroupReadModel row exists (idempotent null guard).

ResourceInstance has a soft-delete flag: DeletedAt (nullable DateTime) at backend/src/Modules/Resources/ThingsBooksy.Modules.Resources.Core/Domain/ResourceInstance.cs:18, with a derived computed property IsDeleted => DeletedAt.HasValue at ResourceInstance.cs:20; DeletedAt is set inside the domain Delete(DateTime) method at ResourceInstance.cs:46.

An EF global query filter excludes soft-deleted ResourceInstances: builder.HasQueryFilter(x => x.DeletedAt == null) is configured in ResourceInstanceConfiguration.Configure at backend/src/Modules/Resources/ThingsBooksy.Modules.Resources.Core/DAL/Configurations/ResourceInstanceConfiguration.cs:15. Both GroupDeletedHandler and DeleteResourceTypeCommandDataProvider.SoftDeleteInstancesAsync explicitly call .IgnoreQueryFilters() before their bulk updates, confirming this filter is active by default and must be bypassed to reach already-soft-deleted rows or to update rows that the filter would otherwise hide during the same operation.
